title: Super Mario Bros. 3 (NES) - World 1-1 physics spec for browser re-implementation
scope: Small and Super (big) Mario on flat ground in World 1-1: walking/running, acceleration/deceleration, jumping, gravity, P-meter, stomping. Raccoon flight, slopes, water, ice and items beyond the Goomba stomp are out of scope except where noted.

units.frame: one NTSC NES frame (about 1/60.0988 s). All timing is in frames; the harness never uses wall-clock time.
units.subpx: 1/16 pixel. SMB3 stores X/Y velocity as 4.4 fixed point: high nibble = whole pixels, low nibble = 1/16 px. A velocity of 40 subpx/frame = 2.5 px/frame.
units.velocity: subpx/frame (1/16 px per frame). px/frame equivalents are given alongside.

confidence.high: read directly from a disassembly constant or code path AND consistent with at least one independent source (or a trivially direct constant)
confidence.medium: single source, or depends on my interpretation of routine ordering / counter phase, or derived by simulation from high-confidence constants

smb1_warning: Do NOT reuse Super Mario Bros. 1 numbers. SMB1 stores vertical speed as whole pixels plus a 1/256 fraction with jump-dependent gravity (e.g. 0x30 rising vs 0xA8 falling) and a 5 px/frame fall clamp, and uses three acceleration magnitudes that double when Mario faces away from his motion. SMB3 uses 4.4 fixed-point velocities, a two-value gravity (1 or 5 subpx/frame^2) and a 4 px/frame fall cap. SMB1 and SMB3 happen to share 1.5 / 2.5 px/frame walk/run caps, which makes the mix-up easy to miss.

t.frame_rate.meaning: NTSC NES frame rate. Use fixed-timestep simulation at this rate (or 60) and step physics per frame.

sources.note: NTSC frame rate is 60.0988 frames per second

v.order.value: apply X vel -> apply Y vel (with fall clamp) -> horizontal control -> jump/gravity -> P-meter -> floor collision -> timers -> enemies/stomp
v.order.meaning: Velocities computed in frame N move Mario in frame N+1. Stomp bounce is set after the player update, so no gravity is added on the stomp frame.

sources.note: Player_ApplyXVelocity / ApplyYVelocity are called before GndMov_* (GroundHControl, JumpFlyFlutter); Player_PowerUpdate and Player_DetectSolids follow (prg008.asm L924-L940)
states that SMB3 applies velocities one frame late
PLAYER_TOPWALKSPEED = $18; comment says velocities are 4.4 fixed point
'If WALKING, the limit is 18' (page convention: values are hex)
Walking/swimming max 24 = 1.5 px/frame

h.run_max.meaning: Top speed while holding B before the P-meter is full (on ground and in air).

sources.note: PLAYER_TOPRUNSPEED = $28
'The limit is raised to 28' (hex)
Run-no P max 40 = 2.5 px/frame

h.pspeed_max.meaning: Top speed while holding B with a full P-meter.

sources.note: PLAYER_TOPPOWERSPEED = $38
'The limit is raised to 38' when P blinks (hex)
Run+P max 56 = 3.5 px/frame

h.abs_max.meaning: Hard clamp applied before moving (only reachable by slopes/sliding; not reachable on flat 1-1 ground).

sources.note: Player_ApplyXVelocity caps |XVel| at PLAYER_MAXSPEED = $40
lists 'Sliding 63' - see conflict C6

h.accel_counter.meaning: A global counter is updated once per frame as W = ((W & 0xF0) - 0x90) & 0xFF, so its high nibble visits all 16 values in a 16-frame cycle. Acceleration/friction add a 'pseudo-fraction' to W and use the carry as a +1/0 decision. This is the 'acceleration framerule' TASers refer to.

sources.note: LDA Counter_Wiggly / AND #$F0 / SUB #$90 / STA Counter_Wiggly, immediately before JSR Player_Update
ADD Counter_Wiggly, carry added to Player_XVel
mentions 'acceleration framerules' that had to line up

h.accel_normal.meaning: Pressing toward the direction of motion below the current cap: +1 subpx/frame on exactly 14 of every 16 consecutive frames (main 0, pseudo-fraction $E0), i.e. 0.875 subpx/frame^2 average. Identical for all ground forms (small/big/fire/leaf) and identical with or without B. Also applies in the air.

sources.note: Player_XAccelMain 'N' column = 0; Player_XAccelPseudoFrac 'N' column = $E0 (L1167) for Small/Big/Fire/Leaf, with and without B
'start to increase ... at around 1 per frame' (exact increment marked to-do); 'same acceleration is always used when walking/running/dashing'
'Holding B makes absolutely no difference to the rate of acceleration or deceleration'

h.accel_normal.confidence_note: 14/16 ratio high; the exact frames of the 2 skipped steps depend on the counter phase (medium) - the harness only checks 16-frame windows, which are phase-independent.

d.skid.meaning: Pressing opposite to the direction of motion (skid/turn): exactly -2 subpx/frame every frame until the velocity sign flips, all forms, ground and air.

sources.note: 'S' (skid) column: main 2, pseudo-fraction $00 (no counter carry possible)
B does not change deceleration

d.friction_small.meaning: No left/right input on the ground, small Mario: -1 on 10 of every 16 frames (main -1, pseudo-fraction $60). Also used when on the ground above the current cap (e.g. B released at 40).

sources.note: 'F' column: Small = $60 (Tanooki/Hammer also $60)

d.friction_big.meaning: Same as d.friction_small for Super/Fire/Raccoon Mario (pseudo-fraction $20): big Mario stops faster than small Mario.

sources.note: 'F' column: Big/Fire/Leaf = $20

d.no_air_friction.meaning: In the air, no input = no deceleration, and being above the current cap (e.g. B released mid-jump at 40) does not slow Mario either. Only skid (-2) or normal acceleration change vx in the air.

sources.note: Player_GroundHControl returns early when Player_InAir is set and no L/R is held, and when over the cap in the air

v.jump_vy.meaning: Base take-off velocity, same for every form. Jump starts only on a NEW press of A while on the ground.

sources.note: PLAYER_JUMP = -$38
'(C8) Initial velocity for player jump' ($C8 = -56)
$AC5A jump power routine
Player_SpeedJumpInc: .byte $00, $02, $04, $08
'Divide by 16 ... using the table 00,02,04,08'

v.gravity_held.meaning: Gravity while airborne, A held and vy < -32 (rising fast). Also applies on the take-off frame itself.

sources.note: $ACA1: 'Y = jump gravity (lower than normal)' = 1 when jump held and v vel still faster than E0
PRG008_ACB3: Y=5; if YVel < -$20 and A held, Y=1; YVel += Y

v.gravity.meaning: Gravity in all other airborne cases (A released, or vy >= -32, or falling).

sources.note: 'LDY #$05 ; Y = default falling gravity'
'(05) Mario falling gravity, added to Y vel each frame'
LDY #$05

v.gravity_threshold.meaning: Light gravity (1) only while vy < -32 (= -2 px/frame). Once vy >= -32 the jump is 'aborted' to gravity 5 even if A is still held.

sources.note: CMP #$E0 ($E0 = -32); jumps aborted when the button is released or 00CF is more positive than E0
CMP #-$20 / BGS (signed)

v.fall_cap.meaning: Before moving each frame, vy >= 64 is clamped to 64, so Mario never falls more than 4 px/frame. Because gravity is added after the move, a RAM/debug readout at end of frame can show up to 69.

sources.note: FALLRATE_MAX = $40, used by Player_ApplyYVelocity (prg008.asm L6941)
'#$40 is the maximum fall vel (note: gravity is added afterwards so the effective value is 45)'
'Nominal falling terminal velocity is 69, but is actually 64' (3Mix hack, same engine)

v.new_press_required.meaning: Holding A through a landing does not re-jump; the jump checks the newly-pressed input, gravity checks the held input.

sources.note: Player_JumpFlyFlutter reads Pad_Input (new presses) for take-off; gravity block reads Pad_Holding

p.levels.meaning: Power is a 7-bit shift register (0, 1, 3, 7, ... $7F). Gain = shift left with a 1; loss = shift right. $7F = full (P flashing).

sources.note: Player_Power: '>>>>>>[P] charge level ($7F max)'
Player_PowerUpdate: SEC/ROL to gain, ROR/LSR to lose

p.run_condition.meaning: An arrow can only be gained on a frame where Mario is on the ground, holding B, not sliding, and |vx| >= 40 (run cap). In the air the meter only drains (unless a P-jump timer is running).

sources.note: GroundHControl: INC Player_RunFlag only if B held, not in air/sliding and |XVel| >= PLAYER_TOPRUNSPEED
'When abs($BD) is >= 28, you are DASHING and the P-timer $515 cycles'

p.gain_period.meaning: While the run condition holds, one arrow every 8 frames. The first arrow comes on the first qualifying frame if the timer is idle. RAM shows the timer as 7 after each gain because it is decremented later in the same frame.

sources.note: LDY #$08 when running, stored to Player_PMeterCnt; counters decremented after Player_Update (L378)
'the P-timer $515 cycles from 7. Every time it elapses an arrow is added'
'$0515 ... 7 if you're running on ground'

p.loss_period.meaning: When not satisfying the run condition (and no P-jump timer), one arrow is lost every 24 frames.

sources.note: LDY #$18 when not running
'the P-timer $515 cycles from 23. Every time it elapses an arrow is removed'
'... and 23 if you're in mid-air'

p.full_hold.meaning: While running at full power the timer is re-armed to 16 every frame (reads 0F in RAM), so the first arrow is lost 16 frames after Mario stops qualifying; later arrows every 24.

sources.note: LDY #$10 at full power while running
'The P-timer is LOCKED to the value 0F'

p.pjump_timer.meaning: Jumping with full power starts a timer that keeps the meter full in the air (Raccoon uses it to fly). Small/Big lose it on landing.

sources.note: 'The flight duration timer $56E is set to 80 and decrements every other frame'
STA Player_FlyTime = $80 when Player_Power = $7F; cleared on ground for forms without flight

s.bounce_vy.meaning: Stomping an enemy sets vy = -64 (stronger than any jump). Normal jump gravity rules then apply, so holding A gives a much higher bounce.

sources.note: 'Set Player's Y velocity to -$40 (bounce!)'

s.stomp_condition.value: vy >= 0, or already killed something this airtime (kill tally > 0)
s.stomp_condition.meaning: Touching an enemy while moving upward hurts Mario unless he has already stomped/killed something since last touching the ground.

sources.note: after the height test: if YVel < 0 and not flying and Kill_Tally = 0 -> hurt

s.stomp_window.meaning: Stomp height test: Player_Y must be at least 19 px above the enemy's Y (17 for two special enemies). With a 32-px player frame for both sizes this means the feet may be at most ~13 px below a 16-px enemy's top. Interpretation of the player frame height is mine.

sources.note: LDY #19 'height above object considered stompable range'

s.chain.meaning: Kill tally increments per stomp without touching the ground; reset on landing. Further stomps after 8000 keep giving 1UPs.

sources.note: score values list; stomp calls Score_Get100PlusPts with Kill_Tally (prg000.asm L3979); Kill_Tally reset on landing (prg008.asm L4651)
first enemy 100, then 200, 400, 800, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, then extra lives

e.walker_vx.meaning: Walking speed of Goomba / Koopa Troopa / Para-Goomba ground walk (ground-troop group).

sources.note: GroundTroop_XVel: -$08, $08 (object IDs $6C-$74 share ObjInit_GroundTroop)

e.object_gravity.meaning: Default object gravity for objects using the standard mover (many enemies write their own).

sources.note: OBJECT_FALL = $03, OBJECT_MAXFALL = $40

e.shell_kick_vx.unit: subpx/frame (+ Mario vx/2 if moving the same way)

sources.note: ObjectKickXVelMoving: -$30, $30; Player_XVel/2 added when same sign

e.mushroom_vx.meaning: Super Mushroom horizontal speed; initial direction chosen from Mario's X (tile parity per the disassembly comment).

sources.note: Mushroom_SetXVel: $10 or -$10

expectations._note: Derived, testable numbers. 'derived' values were computed by stepping the rules above frame by frame (see physics-spec.md, 'Derivations'); tolerance is what the harness allows.

conflicts.topic: Horizontal acceleration (the requested Data Crystal vs TASVideos disagreement)

claims.claim: velocity increases 'at around 1 per frame' (exact increment marked to-do)
acceleration is gated by 'acceleration framerules' that must line up (i.e. not a flat 1/frame)
acceleration needs carefully timed input sequences; B does not change the rate

conflicts.chosen: +1 subpx/frame on 14 of every 16 frames (0.875 average), set by a 16-frame global counter; skid = exactly 2/frame; friction = 10/16 (small) or 14/16 (big).
conflicts.why: The disassembly shows the mechanism that reconciles both: whole-part 0 plus a carry from pseudo-fraction $E0 added to a counter that steps through 16 values. Data Crystal's 'around 1' is this 0.875 average, rounded; the TAS 'framerule' is the 16-frame counter. A literal 1/frame would reach walk speed in 24 frames instead of about 28.

Not a real conflict: Data Crystal states its values are hexadecimal ($18 = 24, $28 = 40, $38 = 56), confirmed by the disassembly constants. Listed because a reader taking '18' as decimal would build a much slower Mario.

claims.claim: max fall $40, 'effective value is 45' because gravity is added afterwards
'Nominal falling terminal velocity is 69, but is actually 64'
Player_ApplyYVelocity clamps to FALLRATE_MAX = $40 before moving

conflicts.chosen: Displacement capped at 64 subpx (4 px) per frame; a velocity readout may legitimately show up to 69.
conflicts.why: All three agree once ordering is considered: clamp-then-move-then-add-gravity. The harness therefore asserts on per-frame displacement, not on the velocity readout.

conflicts.topic: P-meter timer: 7/23 vs 8/24, and which RAM address

claims.claim: address is $0515, not $055D; 7 when running on the ground, 23 in mid-air
timer reloaded with 8 / $18 (24); all such counters decremented after the player update

conflicts.chosen: Gain every 8 frames, loss every 24 frames (timer address $0515).
conflicts.why: 7/23 are the values visible in RAM at end of frame because of the same-frame decrement; the period is reload value = 8/24. Randil's 'mid-air = 23' is the loss timer (the run flag cannot be set in the air). nitsuja's $55D was corrected by Randil and by the disassembly.

conflicts.topic: Meaning of the $E0 value near the gravity code

claims.claim: $E0 is compared against vertical velocity to decide jump gravity

conflicts.chosen: $E0 (-32) is the light-gravity threshold, not a jump velocity; take-off velocity is -56 - bonus.
conflicts.why: The Notes page and the disassembly show it as a CMP operand; the RAM-map line also mislabels ROM addresses as RAM.

conflicts.topic: Absolute X speed cap 63 vs 64 (also 'Flying 23 = 1.958 px/frame')

claims.claim: Sliding max 63 (3.938 px/frame); Flying max 23 listed as 1.958 px/frame

conflicts.why: The TAS table is internally inconsistent (23/16 = 1.4375, not 1.958), so its fine print is weak evidence. 63 may be the practical maximum on slopes. Not tested by the harness.

claims.claim: Counter_Wiggly (the value added to the acceleration pseudo-fraction) sits at $055C; $055D is Counter_7to0

conflicts.chosen: Model the behaviour (16-frame cycle, 14/16 carries); the address is unresolved.
conflicts.why: This does not change any number in the spec. A RAM watch in an emulator would settle which byte TASers meant.
